**Helper wrapping the credential check:** `check_secret` in `src/memory/guard.rs`. It calls `secret_kind` (the actual pattern-matching detector) and formats the `Refused` error if a credential is found.

**Fields it is applied to** — all within the public `check` function in the same file (`src/memory/guard.rs`):

| Field | Line | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | 146 | `check_secret("text", &text)?` |
| `subject` | 156 | `check_secret("subject", s)?` |
| `key` | 160 | `check_secret("key", k)?` |
| each `tag` | 172 | `check_secret("tag", &t)?` |
| each `ref` | 184 | `check_secret("ref", &r)?` |
| `source` | 198 | `check_secret("source", s)?` |

**Files involved:**

- `src/memory/guard.rs` — contains everything: `secret_kind` (the detector, backed by `SECRETS` regex list and `LONG_TOKEN`/`looks_random` entropy check), `check_secret` (the wrapper that turns a detected credential into a `Refused` error), and `check` (the top-level validation entry point that calls `check_secret` for all six field types above).

**Impact of changing the credential check:** Changing `secret_kind`'s detection logic (e.g., adding/removing patterns or adjusting the entropy threshold) automatically affects all six call sites, since they all funnel through `check_secret` → `secret_kind`. Changing `check_secret`'s refusal message format would affect all six field validation paths in `check`. No other files outside `src/memory/guard.rs` contain credential checks.

CONFIDENCE: high
